name: @cloudsforge/hub-api
description: The Forge Hub backend-for-frontend. Composes the dashboard from seven upstreams in one authenticated call, degrades per tile, and owns no state of its own.

scripts._test: No --test-concurrency flag, and no database: this service has neither a pool nor a table to truncate, so test files are free to run in parallel. See the note about migrations below.

_noDatabase: There is no `migrate` script, no migrator, no pool and no SERVICE_DATABASE_URL, and that is
the central design constraint rather than an omission. A BFF that acquires a table acquires a
second copy of somebody else's truth, and the copy is the one that goes stale. Everything this
service serves is fetched from the service that owns it and held in an in-process cache with a
stated TTL; losing the whole cache costs one slow request and nothing else.
The consequence to keep in mind when extending this: a field that exists only here is a bug.
If the dashboard needs a value nobody owns, the fix is a route on the owning service.
_localDependencies: The @cloudsforge/* packages are consumed from sibling checkouts because none of them is
published yet. Once AD-02 lands they all become registry versions and these paths — plus the
build contexts in the Dockerfile and the extra checkouts in CI — are deleted.
Every sibling takes 'link:', not 'file:'. A 'file:' path PACKS the dependency, and each of
these packages declares files: ['dist'] with a publishConfig pointing main/types at dist/.
Packing therefore installs a package whose exports resolve to a dist/ that has not been built.
'link:' symlinks the checkout in place, which is also what @cloudsforge/contracts-money needs:
it depends on contracts-chain with the 'workspace:^' protocol, which resolves only inside the
contracts-chain is here for one reason: confirmation depth. 'progress towards credited' is
confirmations against chainSpec(asset).confirmations, and that number is a contract shared
byte-for-byte with wallet, indexer, custody and settlement. Re-deriving it here would be this
service inventing a fact — the exact failure the no-database rule exists to prevent.
tsx is a runtime dependency because the unpublished packages resolve to TypeScript sources.
